07-24.event: Apollo 11 splashes down in the Pacific. Armstrong, Aldrin and Collins come home from the first Moon landing after eight days in space.

07-25.event: Svetlana Savitskaya becomes the first woman to walk in space, spending 3 hours 35 minutes outside the Salyut 7 station.

07-26.event: Apollo 15 launches from Kennedy Space Center — the first mission to carry a lunar roving vehicle.

07-28.event: Skylab 3 launches, beginning a 59-day stay aboard America's first space station.

07-29.event: President Eisenhower signs the National Aeronautics and Space Act, creating NASA.

07-30.event: Apollo 15's Falcon lands at Hadley Rille, opening the first of the extended J-class science missions on the Moon.

07-31.event: David Scott and James Irwin take the first drive on another world, covering 10 km in the Apollo 15 lunar rover.

08-02.event: Apollo 15's David Scott drops a hammer and a falcon feather on the Moon — both hit the ground together, just as Galileo predicted.

08-03.event: MESSENGER launches on a seven-year journey to become the first spacecraft to orbit Mercury.

08-04.event: Phoenix launches toward the Martian arctic, where it will confirm water ice just below the surface.

08-05.event: Juno launches toward Jupiter. Five years later it enters polar orbit around the largest planet in the solar system.

08-06.event: Curiosity lands in Gale Crater after the 'seven minutes of terror' sky-crane descent — the largest rover ever sent to Mars at the time.

08-07.event: Explorer 6 launches and returns the first photograph of Earth taken from orbit.

08-09.event: Luna 24 launches — the Soviet Union's last Moon mission, and the last robotic lunar sample return for 44 years.

08-10.event: Magellan arrives at Venus and begins mapping 98 percent of the planet's surface with radar.

08-11.event: Vostok 3 launches with Andriyan Nikolayev. A day later Vostok 4 follows — the first time two crewed spacecraft fly in orbit at once.

08-12.event: Parker Solar Probe launches, on its way to fly through the Sun's corona and become the fastest spacecraft ever built.

08-17.event: Venera 7 launches. In December it becomes the first spacecraft to land on another planet and transmit from the surface of Venus.

08-19.event: Sputnik 5 carries the dogs Belka and Strelka to orbit — the first living creatures recovered safely from space.

08-20.event: Voyager 2 launches. Forty-nine years later it is still transmitting, from beyond the edge of the heliosphere.

08-21.event: Gemini 5 launches on the first week-long American spaceflight, proving crews could endure a trip to the Moon and back.

08-23.event: Lunar Orbiter 1 takes the first photograph of Earth as seen from the Moon.

08-25.event: Voyager 1 crosses into interstellar space — the first human-made object to leave the heliosphere.

08-30.event: STS-8 launches with Guion Bluford, the first African American in space, aboard Challenger's first night launch.

09-03.event: Viking 2 lands on Utopia Planitia, joining Viking 1 for the first sustained robotic science campaign on Mars.

09-05.event: Voyager 1 launches — sixteen days after its twin, but on a faster path that will carry it farther than any spacecraft in history.

09-08.event: OSIRIS-REx launches toward asteroid Bennu, beginning America's first asteroid sample return mission.

09-12.event: President Kennedy at Rice University: 'We choose to go to the Moon in this decade and do the other things, not because they are easy, but because they are hard.'

09-15.event: Cassini ends 13 years at Saturn with a deliberate plunge into the planet's atmosphere, transmitting to the last second.

09-21.event: Galileo is deliberately flown into Jupiter after 14 years, protecting the possibly habitable moon Europa from contamination.

09-26.event: DART slams into the asteroid moon Dimorphos at 22,000 km/h — the first deliberate test of planetary defense, and it worked.

09-28.event: SpaceX's Falcon 1 reaches orbit on its fourth attempt — the first privately developed liquid-fueled rocket to do so.

09-29.event: Discovery launches on STS-26, returning the shuttle to flight 32 months after the Challenger accident.

09-30.event: Rosetta ends its mission with a controlled descent onto comet 67P, joining the Philae lander it delivered two years earlier.
